objective: Managing PMO services in production: phased rollout for high-impact services, clear delivery workflows, and escalation procedures
secondaryObjectives: Onboarding new PMO service customers: a structured onboarding process, documentation, and a support system during ramp-up

sources.cite: PMI, PMI PMO Certified Professional (PMI-PMOCP) Examination Content Outline and Specifications, January 2025 (v2): Organizational Development and Alignment 16%, PMO Strategic Elements 18%, PMO Design and Structuring 18%, PMO Operation and Performance 15%, PMO Enhancement and Effectiveness 18%, People 15%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a study page (masteryexamprep, dated 2025-12-20) that cites PMI's outline of January 2025 (v2) for these weights. The page lists no task statements; it says questions reward 'governance realism: decision rights, thresholds, escalation paths, and reporting that drives decisions'. PMI's PDF (the course seed cites it) was not opened; the task wording is the course seed's, to verify. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's water-utility-rebalance-pmipmocp (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: Your PMO at Wexford Logistics, a fictional company, is launching a resource capacity service that every functional manager will rely on for staffing decisions.
handover: The capacity tool pulls from HR and timesheets.
Forty functional managers are waiting for it.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: managers in two departments see colleagues 'available' who are fully booked and double-book them on client work.
Week 3: managers misread 'tentative' as 'available' and staff a client project with people on leave.
Week 4: other directors hear and stop using the service.

choices.label: Roll out to two departments with good data first, fix the timesheet gaps, then the rest in waves
choices.feedback: High-impact services roll out in phases so problems hit few customers.

choices.label: Launch to half the managers
choices.feedback: Half includes the departments with bad data.

choices.label: Launch to all forty at once
choices.feedback: Bad data reaches every manager at once.

choices.label: A structured onboarding session, a short guide, a named contact and a weekly office hour during ramp-up
choices.feedback: Onboarding and support during ramp-up make a service usable.

escPrompt.title: A director disputes the data
escPrompt.context: A director says the tool shows his team as idle while they're overloaded.

choices.label: Use the escalation procedure: log it, confirm the data cause within the SLA, fix it, and report the resolution to the director and the sponsor

effects.log: The issue is resolved within the SLA.

choices.feedback: Defined escalation procedures resolve production issues predictably.

choices.label: Fix it quietly yourself
choices.feedback: Fixed, but the cause isn't recorded and others are affected.

choices.label: Tell the director the tool is right
choices.feedback: The data was wrong; trust in the service collapses.

reflection.question: Write the operations record for the PMO sponsor.

parts.label: Rollout and onboarding
parts.criteria: Phased from good-data departments; onboarding, a contact and office hours.
parts.modelAnswer: We started with two departments with good data, fixed the gaps, then rolled out in waves, with onboarding and a named contact.

parts.label: Escalation
parts.criteria: Procedure: logged, cause found, fixed and reported.
parts.modelAnswer: The director's dispute was logged, traced to missing timesheets, fixed within the SLA and reported.

source.note: No risk above appetite at the close without a treatment.

expertPath.text: Review data quality and the rollout plan first.
Roll out in phases, starting where data is good.
Onboard managers with a guide, a contact and office hours.
Escalate per the procedure and report the resolution.

scoring.modelReasoning: PMO services in production are rolled out in phases when their impact is high, supported by structured onboarding during ramp-up, and run with clear delivery workflows and escalation procedures so problems are resolved predictably and visibly.
